newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks end down on first trade day under China.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end down on first trade day under China.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slumped on their first trading day under Chinese rule on Thursday, unable to retain the momentum of an early surge to record highs as worries about the property market stamped out handover optimism.
The Hang Seng Index closed down 141.05 points, or 0.93 percent, at 15,055.74 after surging to an all-time high of 15,363.61 within minutes of the opening bell.

"Because of the handover holiday mood, local investors just pushed up the market but the sell orders from the institutional side were much bigger," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP PrimeEast Securities.
The red chip Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index ended 55.82 points, or 1.61 percent, lower at 3,413.50.
Turnover was a heavy HK$24.5 billion compared with HK$26.02 billion last Friday.
The market was closed on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday to mark Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

"The market surged this morning because people thought that it would open higher due to the change in sovereignty and Chinese funds bidding shares higher," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities. "It did happen but resistance at this level is very great and people began to take profits."

Property stocks led the blue chips down after Hong Kong Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa said in his inaugural address on Tuesday that his new administration would increase housing supply to tackle spiralling property prices.

Analysts said in the absence of specific policy details on housing, investors were likely to remain cautious on the property sector. "Tung said that he will do something in the property market but nobody knows what he will do," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.
Shares in Cheung Kong tumbled HK$2.75 to HK$73.75 and Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$4.50 to HK$88.75.

Banks bucked the trend with HSBC Holdings soaring to a new all-time high at HK$239.00 before ending the session up HK$5.00 at HK$238.00. Hang Seng Bank also hit a record high at HK$117.00 before ending up HK$4.00 at HK$114.50.
"If you are still bullish on the Hong Kong market but uncertain about property, you go into banks," said Tang.
Analysts said the Hong Kong market had also suffered on Thursday from some switching into Thailand after the de facto devaluation of the baht made Thai equities more attractive.
They said the Hong Kong market could consolidate in coming days before moving higher.
